Operation Dynamo , the Allied evacuation of 340,000 troops from Dunkirk , begins. The move will last until June 3 under ferocious bombardment by the Luftwaffe.
In the North Atlantic, Royal Navy Fairey Swordfish aircraft from the carrier HMS  Ark Royal fatally cripple the Bismarck in torpedo attack.

The Anglo-Soviet Treaty: their foreign secretaries agree that no peace will be signed by one without the approval of the other. (An important treaty since Himmler and others will attempt to separate the two nations at th

05-28.text: Belgium surrenders to the Germans; King Leopold III of Belgium surrenders and is interned.
British and Commonwealth forces begin to evacuate Crete.
By this date, it is clear that operation "Brevity" has failed.

05-30.text: Crucial British Cabinet meeting: Churchill wins a vote on continuing the war, in spite of vigorous arguments by Lord Halifax and Chamberlain.
The pro-Axis Iraqi leader Rashid Ali al-Gaylani and his supporters, including Amin al-Husseini , flee Iraq as British troops approach Baghdad.
"The Thousand Bomber Raid" on Cologne, revealing new area bombing techniques.
Attu Island is again under American control as the Battle of Attu concludes.

05-31.text: The Japanese heavily bomb the Chinese Nationalist capital of Chongqing , on the upper Yangtze .
Heavy Luftwaffe bombing on neutral Ireland's capital ; numerous civilian casualties.
The Mayor of Baghdad surrenders the city to British forces and ends the Anglo-Iraqi War.
Huge German successes around Kharkov, with envelopment of several Red Army armies.
The Japanese retreat from Imphal (India) with heavy losses; their invasion of India is over.

06-03.text: Last day of Operation Dynamo. 224,686 British and 121,445 French and Belgian troops have been evacuated.
The British coal industry is nationalised.
There are daily bombings of the Cherbourg peninsula and the Normandy area. : The provisional French government is established

06-04.text: Winston Churchill delivers his, " We shall fight on the beaches ...we shall never surrender" speech to the House of Commons.
Kaiser William II , former German Emperor, dies in exile in the Netherlands.
In the Battle of Midway , the day opens with Admiral Nagumo's attack on the air defences of the island.
General Henri Giraud becomes Commander-in-Chief of the Free French forces.

Allies enter Rome , one day after the Germans declared it an open city . German troops fall back to the Trasimene Line . : Operation Overlord is postponed 24 hours due to high seas. German U-505 is captured by US forces,

06-07.text: German battleships Gneisenau and Scharnhorst sink the aircraft carrier HMS Glorious and two destroyers off Norway; the British ships have had no air cover.
In the Aleutian Islands, Japanese forces invade Attu and Kiska . This is the first invasion of American soil in 128 years. Japanese occupation of Attu and Kiska begins.
Bayeux is liberated by British troops.

06-09.text: Red Army provokes conflicts on the Latvian border.
Finland initiates mobilisation, preparations against possible attack of Soviet aggressor.

The British and Australians cross the Litani River , beating back Vichy French forces. During this battle, Moshe Dayan , leading an Australian unit, loses his eye. He becomes famous when his story is published a day late

At Bir Hakeim , Rommel renews his attacks on the 1st Free French Brigade's "box". Although the Free French continue to hold out, their perimeter, never the largest, is dangerously reduced in size, and their position beco

No agreement having been reached on their mutual borders, Soviet forces launch an offensive against Finland with the intent of defeating Finland before pushing for Berlin . 6 June 1944: A Navy LCVP disembarks troops at O

06-10.text: Italy declares war on France and the United Kingdom. Norway surrenders after 2 months of combat, the longest of any nation that had been invaded by Germany. King Haakon and his government had evacuated to Britain three d
Assab , the last Italian-held port in East Africa, falls.
Nazis burn the Czech village of Lidice as reprisal for the killing of Reinhard Heydrich . All male adults and children are killed, and all females are taken off to concentration camps.

06-11.text: Two convoys set out for Malta , one from Gibraltar (code named 'Harpoon' ) and the other from Alexandria (code named 'Vigorous' ), with desperately needed supplies of food, fuel, and ammunition. The hope is that the Axis
British 1st Division takes the Italian island of Pantelleria , between Tunisia and Sicily, capturing 11,000 Italian troops.
Schiermonnikoog , a Dutch island, is the last part of Europe freed by Allied troops.

06-12.text: More than 10,000 British soldiers of the 51st (Highland) Division are captured at Saint-Valéry-en-Caux .
Heavy fighting in Sevastopol with serious losses of life on both sides.
The Italian island of Lampedusa , between Tunisia and Sicily, surrenders to the Allies.
American aircraft carriers commence air strikes on the Marianas , including Saipan , preparing for invasion.

06-13.text: The French government moves again, this time to Bordeaux .
The Australians continue to fight through the Vichy French defenses and advance towards Beirut, winning the Battle of Jezzine .
Soviets begin deporting Lithuanians to Siberia. Deportations continue for five days and total 35,000 Lithuanians, among them 7000 Jews.
The United States opens its Office of War Information , a centre to coordinate and properly disseminated wartime information from the military/administration to the public .
Heavy US aircraft losses over Kiel .

Germany launches a V1 Flying Bomb attack on England , in Hitler's view a kind of revenge for the invasion. He believes in Germany's victory with this "secret weapon". The V-1 attacks will continue through October, when t
The Australians capture Brunei . : Japanese Admiral Ota Minoru , along with thousands of his surrounded Naval brigade, commits ritual suicide for failing to defend Okinawa, Japan.

06-14.text: Paris occupied by German troops; Elements of the French Navy ( Marine Nationale ) based in Toulon carried out offensive operations against Italian targets along the Ligurian coast .

A total military blockade on the Baltic States by the Soviet Baltic Fleet . Soviet troops along the Baltic borders are ready to organise communist coups in the Baltic States. Soviet bombers shoot down a Finnish passenger
All German and Italian assets in the United States are frozen.
At the Gazala Line , the British position has become untenable, and General Auchinleck authorizes General Ritchie to make a concerted withdrawal from forward positions along the line.

06-15.text: Eight-hour ultimatum to surrender is given to Lithuania by the Soviets. President Smetona escapes from the country so the takeover is not possible to do in a formally legal way. Soviet troops enter Lithuania and attack L
Start of the evacuation of British troops from ports in western France in Operation Aerial .
British Operation Battleaxe attempts and fails to relieve the Siege of Tobruk . The British are heavily defeated at Halfaya Pass nicknamed "Hell-fire pass".
General Auchinleck sends Churchill a reply to the latter's telegram of the 14th, saying in part, "...I have no intention whatever of giving up Tobruk."
U.S. Marine and Army forces invade the island of Saipan . U.S. submarines sight the Japanese fleet en route.

06-16.text: Philippe Pétain becomes premier of France upon the resignation of Reynaud's government.
The French sloop La Curieuse forces the Italian submarine Provano to surface and then sinks it by ramming.
Soviet Union gives eight-hour ultimatum to Latvia and Estonia to surrender.
All German and Italian consulates in the United States are ordered closed and their staffs to leave the country by July 10.

Two convoys moving toward Malta suffer heavy losses; German air forces continue to bomb the island itself. Operation Harpoon arrives in Malta , but only two of the six supply ships survive; one of them has lost part of i
The Japanese are in a general retreat in central China.

06-17.text: Sinking of liner RMS Lancastria off St Nazaire while being used as a British troopship— 5000-7000 are killed in Britain's worst maritime disaster.
Soviet troops enter Latvia and Estonia.
Allies bomb Sicily and the Italian mainland, as signs increase of a forthcoming invasion.
Free French troops land on Elba .

06-18.text: General De Gaulle forms the Comité français de la Libération nationale , a French government in exile.
Estonia , Latvia and Lithuania are occupied by the Soviet Union.
The Manhattan Project is started, the beginning of a scientific approach to nuclear weapons in the US, building on research work done in the UK.
Elba is declared liberated. : Allies capture Assisi , Italy.

06-20.text: The French seek an armistice with the Italians.

Under the directives of the United States Department of War , the bulk of the personnel of what had been known as the United States Army Air Corps up to this date are brought into what becomes the United States Army Air
The British take Perugia , Italy. : The Siege of Imphal is lifted after three months.

06-21.text: Franco-German armistice negotiations begin at Compiègne .
Elements of two Italian armies cross into France during Italian invasion of France .

The French battleship Lorraine opened fire on the Italian port of Bardia in Italian North Africa . During some of the last actions of the French against the Italians, French naval aircraft attacked Taranto and Livorno in
Soviet-led coups in the Baltic States. In the only military resistance in Tallinn, 2 die on Estonian side and about 10 on the Soviet side.
President Roosevelt authorizes $6,000 For Executive Order 8807 (Manhattan Project-Nuclear Weapons).

Afrika Korps recaptures Tobruk, with 35,000 men captured; the road to Egypt is now open as the British retreat deep into Egypt. Tobruk's loss is a grievous blow to British morale. German land forces have been assisted by

Operation Cartwheel opens with landings by the United States 4th Marine Raider Battalion at Segi Point on New Georgia in the Solomon Islands, beginning the New Georgia Campaign . It will not be secured until August.

06-22.text: Germany invades the Soviet Union with Operation Barbarossa , a three-pronged operation aimed at Leningrad, Moscow, and the southern oil fields of the Caucasus, ending the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact . Romania invades south-w
British general in Libya/Egypt Wavell is replaced by General Auchinleck.
June Uprising against the Soviet Union in Lithuania .

V-1s continue to hit England, especially London, sometimes with horrifying losses. : Operation Bagration : General attack by Soviet forces to clear the German forces from Belarus This results in the destruction of the Ge
The defeat of the Japanese on Okinawa is now complete.

06-24.text: German forces enter Vilnius . Lithuanian militia men go on a shooting spree, killing dozens of Jews on the streets, with civilian spectators cheering them on. The Germans kidnap 60 Jewish "hostages" and 30 Poles. Only 6
General Dwight D. Eisenhower arrives in London ready to assume the post of Commander of American forces in Europe .
Continuing attacks against the Ruhr industrial valley. One result is the evacuation of large numbers of German civilians from the area.

06-25.text: France officially surrenders to Germany at 01:35.
Last major evacuation of Operation Aerial ; 191,870 Allied soldiers, airmen and some civilians had escaped from France.
The Soviet Union bombs Helsinki. Finland pronounces a state of war between Finland and Soviet Union.
163rd Infantry Division (Wehrmacht) starts to travel through Sweden .
Another massive British "Thousand Bomber" raid, this time on Bremen ; the raiders suffer grievous losses.
The Battle of Tali-Ihantala between Finnish and Soviet troops begins. Largest battle ever to be fought in the Nordic countries .

06-26.text: The Soviet Union sends an ultimatum demanding Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina from Romania.
Hungary and Slovakia declare war on the Soviet Union.
Cherbourg is liberated by American troops.
The United Nations Charter is signed in San Francisco.

06-27.text: Romanians propose negotiations. Molotov replies that the demands are land concessions or war. New ultimatum from the Soviets to the Romanians.
The occupation of Lithuania starts officially.
Convoy PQ 17 sets sail from Iceland; only 11 of 37 ships will survive.
San Marino is bombed by the Allies, under the belief that Axis forces had been stationed there
The first oil pump is restored at Tarakan Island .

06-28.text: General De Gaulle recognised by British as leader of Free French .
Marshal Italo Balbo , Commander-in-Chief of Italian North Africa , is accidentally killed in a " friendly fire incident " by Italian anti-aircraft fire at Tobruk, Libya.
The Red Army occupies Romanian Bessarabia and the northern part of Bukovina.

The Luftwaffe bombs the demilitarised British Channel Islands, they had not been informed of the demilitarization. In Guernsey, 33 are killed and 67 injured, in Jersey, 9 are killed and many are injured.
Axis and Allied convoys clash south-west of Crete .
Italian-occupied Albania declares war on the Soviet Union.
Huge German encirclement of 300,000 Red Army troops near Minsk and Białystok .
Case Blue , the German plan to capture Stalingrad and the Soviet Union oil fields in the Caucasus , begins. Generally, forces are shifted to the South.

06-29.text: Japanese Foreign Minister Hachiro Arita announces Japans intention to establish a bloc of Asian nations led by the Japanese and free from western powers .
Finnish and German troops begin Operation Arctic Fox against the Soviet Union.
Nuremberg Laws imposed on Jews of Lithuania and Vilnius in particular.

06-30.text: United States deploys II Corps to the European Theater.
American troops land on Rendova Island , New Georgia, another part of Operation Cartwheel.

07-01.text: Channel Islands occupation is completed by German forces.
Marshal Rodolfo Graziani is named as Balbo's replacement in North Africa.
The Italian Royal Air Force starts bombing the British Mandate of Palestine .
General Auchinleck takes over from General Wavell in North Africa.
The British win the Battle of Palmyra against the French in the Middle East.
All American men over 21 are required to register for the draft.
German troops occupy Latvia's capital, Riga , on the way to Leningrad.
First Battle of El Alamein begins as Rommel begins first assault on British defences.
The Leningrad diarist Tanya Savicheva dies of starvation at the age of 14. Her diary of her family's death during the siege becomes famous.
Australian troops land at Balikpapan, Borneo in the Western Allies' last major land operation of the war.

07-02.text: Hitler orders preparation of plans for invasion of Britain, code-named Operation Sea Lion .
Brighton beach is closed to the public and mines, barbed wire and other defences are put into place.
Hungarian troops take over Stanisławów and other towns in what is now Ukraine.
Churchill survives a censure motion in the House of Commons.
V-1s continue to have devastating effects in South-East England in terms of material destruction and losses of life.

07-03.text: Cardiff is bombed by the Luftwaffe for the first time.

The French Fleet at Mers-el-Kébir is attacked by the Royal Navy 's Force H . The Vichy French government breaks off diplomatic relations with Britain in protest. At Alexandria, the French agree to demilitarise their east
Stalin announces a " scorched earth policy ".
Estonian Forest Brothers start offensives against the Red Army in Southern Estonia, several days before the arrival of German forces. This marks the beginning of the Summer War in Estonia.
The United States of America elevates its General Headquarters, United States Army in order to command and plan for military operations within the Zone of the Interior .
Italian General Pietro Gazzera surrenders the remnants of his forces in the Jimma area of Ethiopia.
British troops employ brave and risky flanking tactics to win the Battle of Deir ez-Zor .
Guadalcanal is now firmly in the hands of the Japanese.

Minsk in Belarus is liberated by Soviet forces. : The Allies find themselves in the "battle of the hedgerows ", as they are stymied by the agricultural hedges in Western France which intelligence had not properly evaluat

07-04.text: The Duke of Windsor (tainted by suspicion of pro-Nazism) is named 56th governor of the Bahamas , putting him some distance from controversy.
Sark surrenders to the Germans. The Germans now control all of the British Channel Islands.

The German News Bureau released excerpts of the documents captured during the fall of France relating to Operation Pike , an Anglo-French plan to bomb Soviet oil fields. The compromised operation was subsequently aborted
Mass murder of Polish scientists and writers , committed by German troops in captured Polish city of Lwów .
US intelligence through its MAGIC intercepts discover Japanese plans to attack South East Asia.
First air missions by the United States Army Air Forces in Europe.
Exiled Polish leader General Władysław Sikorski dies in an air crash in Gibraltar.

07-05.text: Two Belgian politicians, Camille Huysmans and Marcel-Henri Jaspar , form an unofficial government in exile in London, afraid that the official Belgian government , still in France, will surrender to the Germans.
British Government rules out possibility of negotiated peace with Nazi Germany.
British torpedo planes sink an Italian destroyer at Tobruk; on the 20th, two more are sunk.
First German forces enter Estonia from Latvia.
German troops reach the Dnieper River.
Operation Citadel (the Battle of Kursk ) begins. : Conclusion of the National Bands Agreement in occupied Greece , which is to coordinate the actions of the Resistance movement in Greece.
General Douglas MacArthur announces that the Philippines have been liberated.

07-09.text: A fairly indecisive naval skirmish happens off the coast of Italy. No ships are lost.
Vitebsk (Belarus) is captured; this opens the battle of Smolensk , an important communications centre, considered by the German high command to be "the gateway to Moscow."

After heavy resistance Caen , France, is liberated by the British troops on the left flank of the Allied advance. : Saipan is declared secure, the Japanese having lost over 30,000 troops; in the last stages numerous civi

07-10.text: The Battle of Britain begins with Luftwaffe raids on channel shipping.
President Roosevelt asks Congress for huge increases in military preparations.

The Red Army takes up positions on the Emajõgi River line, allowing Estonian Forest Brothers to take control over Southeastern Estonia, including in most of Tartu , where the NKVD executes 193 prisoners and the Red Army
The occupation of Latvia starts officially. Guderian's Panzers take Minsk ; the Germans advance farther into Ukraine.
Units of the Italian Expeditionary Corps in Russia begin to arrive. A legion from the Independent State of Croatia is part of the Italian corps.
Operation Husky (the Allied invasion of Sicily ) begins.
Japanese are still resisting on New Guinea . : Tokyo is bombed for the first time since the Doolittle raid of April 1942.
US Navy Fast Carrier Task Force 38 aircraft participate in attacks on Tokyo for the first time.

07-11.text: RAF raids on enemy emplacements in the Netherlands and on German munitions factories.
Rommel's forces are now stalemated before El Alamein, largely because of a lack of ammunition.
President Roosevelt announces that he will run for an unprecedented fourth term as U.S. President.

07-12.text: Luftwaffe attacks on Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
The Vichy French surrender in Syria.
Assistance Pact signed between the United Kingdom and the USSR.
It now becomes clear that Stalingrad is the largest challenge to the invaders.
/:13: Off the Solomon Islands, the Japanese win a tactical victory at the Battle of Kolombangara .
The Battle of Prokhorovka begins; the largest tank battle in human history and part of the Battle of Kursk, it is the pivotal battle of Operation Citadel.
Hitler rejects General Field Marshal Walther Model 's proposal to withdraw the German forces from Estonia and northern Latvia and retreat to the Daugava River .

07-14.text: Soviets organize rigged elections in the Baltic States. The parliaments will be in the control of the Soviets.

07-16.text: Adolf Hitler submits to his military the directive for the invasion of the United Kingdom, Operation Sea Lion .
German Panzers under Guderian reach Smolensk, increasing the risk to Moscow.

Vel' d'Hiv Roundup : On order from the Vichy France government headed by Pierre Laval , French police officers mass arrest 13,152 Jews and hold them at the Winter Velodrome before deportation to Auschwitz .
First troops of the Brazilian Expeditionary Force (FEB) arrive in Italy.
The U.S. conducts the Trinity test at Alamogordo, New Mexico , the first test of a nuclear weapon .

07-18.text: In response to Mers-el-Kébir, the Vichy French Air Force bombs British-held Gibraltar .
The Germans test fly the Messerschmitt Me 262 V3 third prototype using only its jet engines for the first time.

General Hideki Tojo resigns as chief minister of the Japanese government as the defeats of the Japanese military forces continue to mount. Emperor Hirohito asks General Kuniaki Koiso to form a new government. : Saint-Lô

07-19.text: Allied ships clash with two Italian light cruisers, sinking one in the Battle of Cape Spada .
The " V-sign ", displayed most notably by Churchill, is unofficially adopted as the Allied signal, along with the motif of Beethoven's Fifth Symphony .

Battle of the Atlantic : German Grand Admiral Karl Dönitz orders the last U-boats to withdraw from their United States Atlantic coast positions in response to an increasingly effective American convoy system.
The Allies bomb Rome for the first time.
American forces take Leghorn ( Livorno ), Italy far up the Italian boot.

07-21.text: Czechoslovak government in exile arrives in London.
In the Baltic States Soviet controlled parliaments request membership of USSR.
The Luftwaffe strikes heavily at Moscow.
The Operation Bellicose targeting of Friedrichshafen Würzburg radars is the first bombing of a V-2 rocket facility.

07-22.text: The Havana Conference meets; the nations of the Western hemisphere meet to discuss neutrality and economic cooperation.
Fumimaro Konoye is named the Prime Minister of Japan.
U.S. forces under Patton capture Palermo , Sicily.
Hitler gives permission to retreat from the Narva River to the Tannenberg defence line in the Sinimäed Hills 20 km west from Narva.
America and Japan engage in a small skirmish in the Battle of Tokyo Bay . The Japanese take slight losses Clement Attlee , Harry S. Truman and Joseph Stalin at the 1945 Potsdam Conference .

07-23.text: The British " Home Guard " is officially established, drawing on elderly men and those considered unable to serve in the regular armed forces.
Germans take Rostov-on-the-Don; the Red Army is in a general retreat along the Don River.
The USAAF orders the first 100 examples of the planned Convair B-36 six-engined intercontinental strategic bomber.
The Poles rise up against the Germans in the Lwow Uprising .

07-25.text: All women and children are ordered to evacuate Gibraltar .
Mussolini is arrested and relieved of his offices after a meeting with Italian King Victor Emmanuel III , who chooses Marshal Pietro Badoglio to form a new government.

In response to the Japanese occupation of French Indochina , US President Franklin D. Roosevelt orders the seizure of all Japanese assets in the United States.
Germans order a Judenrat established in Stanisławów, Galicia . It is headed by Israel Seibald.
A second attack by the British under Auchinleck fails against Rommel. First Battle of El Alamein may be said to be over.

The first aerial victory for a jet fighter occurs, with an Me 262 of the Luftwaffe's Ekdo 262 damaging a de Havilland Mosquito reconnaissance aircraft of the Royal Air Force's No. 540 Squadron RAF . : The Leningrad Front

The Labour Party win the British general election by a landslide. Clement Attlee replaces Churchill as British Prime Minister and immediately flies to the negotiating table at Potsdam. The Potsdam Declaration is issued.

Hitler sets 15 September as the date for Operation Sea Lion , the invasion of Britain.

The Italian Royal Navy establishes its BETASOM submarine base in Bordeaux and joins the " Battle of the Atlantic ."
4 August: Operation Hurry, the first of the Malta Convoys , is accomplished.
The US announces an oil embargo against "aggressors".
The Germans declare Galicia as the fifth district of the Generalgouvernement .
The Germans continue their successful advance toward Stalingrad.
Operation Tidal Wave : Oil refineries at Ploiești , Romania , are bombed by U.S. IX Bomber Command . : Japan declares independence for the State of Burma under Ba Maw .

The Warsaw Uprising , staged by the Polish Home Army , begins: the Polish people rise up, expecting aid from the approaching Soviet Union armies, but it never comes. : The Red Army isolates the Baltic States from East Pr
Ukrainian insurgents attack the police station in Baligrod , Poland . Polish soldiers defend the station, driving off the attackers, who torch several houses as they retreat.

08-02.text: General Charles de Gaulle sentenced to death in absentia by a French military court.
The USSR annexes Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina .
All civilian radios in Norway confiscated by the German occupation.

SS Commander Hans Krueger (alternative spelling, Hans Krüger) orders the registration of hundreds of Jewish and Polish intelligentsia in Stanisławów , who are subsequently tortured and murdered. This is the first impleme
2,897 Romani are gassed when their camp at Auschwitz is liquidated. : John F. Kennedy's PT-109 is rammed in two and sunk off the Solomon Islands .
End of the Potsdam Conference : Issues such as the expulsion of Germans from the eastern quarter of Germany and elsewhere in eastern Europe are mandated in the Potsdam Agreement .

08-03.text: A convoy to Malta is decimated by the Luftwaffe and U-boats.
The first of two " George S. Patton slapping incidents " occurs in Sicily.
Allied U.S. and Chinese troops under Stilwell overcome a vigorous Japanese defense and take Myitkyina , in northern Burma.

08-04.text: Italian forces under General Guglielmo Nasi invade and occupy British Somaliland during the East African Campaign .

Florence is liberated by the Allies, particularly British and South African troops. Before exiting, the Germans under General Albert Kesselring destroy some historic bridges and historically valuable buildings. : Rennes

08-05.text: Failure to achieve air superiority and bad weather in the Channel results in a postponement of the invasion of Great Britain.
German armies trap Red Army forces in Smolensk pocket and take 300,000 soldiers; Orel is taken.

The U.S. planning team for Operation Torch , which includes George S. Patton ; Jimmy Doolittle ; and Hoyt S. Vandenberg , meets in Washington, D.C. to join the combined planning team from London, England. : Henrik Hersch
Swedish government announces it will no longer allow German troops and war material to transit Swedish railways . : Russians recapture Orel and Belgorod .

08-06.text: American and British governments warn Japan not to invade Thailand .
German troops start pouring in to take over Italy's defences.
The B-29 bomber Enola Gay drops the first atomic bomb " Little Boy " on Hiroshima .

08-11.text: 15 August: Battle of Tug Argan fought in British Somaliland during the Italian invasion . To avoid encirclement, the British withdraw.
Malta is relieved by a convoy.
Chungking, the nominal capital of Nationalist China located far up the Yangtze River, suffers several days of heavy bombing.
HMS  Eagle , a carrier on convoy duty to Malta, is torpedoed and sinks with heavy loss of life.
German and Italian forces begin to evacuate Sicily.

08-13.text: This is " Adler Tag " or "Eagle Day". Hermann Göring starts a two-week assault on British airfields in preparation for invasion. (For some German historians, this is the beginning of the " Battle of Britain .")

General Bernard Montgomery appointed commander of the Eighth Army, which encompassed Allied ground forces in Egypt and Libya; Churchill is anxious to see more offensive action on the part of the Allies in North Africa.

The failure of the Allies to close the Falaise pocket in France proves advantageous to the Germans fleeing to the east who escape the pincer movement of the Allies. : A clash between Italian POWs and American servicemen

Japanese military personnel and right-wingers attempt to overthrow their government and prevent the inevitable surrender. : The last day of United States Force combat actions. All units are frozen in place. Eritrean news

08-15.text: RAF victories over the Luftwaffe continue, in a wide-ranging fight along the East coast. British fighter aircraft production begins to accelerate.
Sinking of the Greek cruiser Elli by an Italian submarine on 15 August 1940 at the harbour of Tinos .
Malta is supplied via Operation Pedestal .
The Land Battle of Vella Lavella island in the Solomons begins. : US and Canadian troops invade Kiska Island in the Aleutians, not knowing the Japanese have already evacuated.
Operation Dragoon begins, marked by amphibious Allied landings in southern France . : The Allies reach the "Gothic Line", the last German strategic position in North Italy.

Emperor Hirohito issues a radio broadcast announcing the Surrender of Japan ; though the surrender seems to be "unconditional", the Emperor's status is still open for discussion. : Victory over Japan Day celebrations tak

08-16.text: The Battle of Britain continues; Germans are hampered by poor aircraft range and British extensive use of RADAR.
A first draft of the Destroyers for Bases Agreement by the US and Britain is made public.
Polish Jews begin a resistance with scant weaponry in Białystok . The leaders commit suicide when they run out of ammunition. : U.S. troops enter Messina , Sicily.

Emperor Hirohito issues an Imperial Rescript ordering Japanese forces to cease fire. The Fat Man mushroom cloud resulting from the nuclear explosion over Nagasaki rises 18 km (60,000 ft) into the air from the hypocentre

08-17.text: Hitler declares a blockade of the British Isles.
German forces capture Narva in Northeastern Estonia, leaving the Red Army in control of only its pocket in Northwestern Estonia and the West Estonian archipelago.
First US Army Air Forces B-17 heavy bomber raid in Europe, targeting the Sotteville railroad yards at Rouen, France.

All of Sicily now controlled by the Allies. : Heavy loss of Allied bombers in the Schweinfurt–Regensburg mission . : Operation Crossbow begins with Operation Hydra when the RAF bombs the Peenemünde V-2 rocket facility.
Indonesia declares independence from Japan and beginning a national revolution . : General Order No. 1 for the surrender of Japan is approved by President Truman.

In New Guinea, both Japanese and Australian reinforcements arrive.

Operation Jubilee , a raid by British and Canadian forces on Dieppe, France , ends in disaster; they come under heavy gunfire and eventually most are killed or captured by the German defenders.
Roosevelt and Churchill signed the Quebec Agreement during the Quebec Conference .

Churchill's speech " Never was so much owed by so many to so few " speech delivered to the House of Commons .
Chinese Communists launch the Hundred Regiments Offensive against the Japanese in North China.
German 250th Infantry Division, nicknamed "Blue Division" and consisting of Spanish volunteers, was formed and began to move to Poland.
Henderson Field on Guadalcanal receives its first American fighter planes.
The Red Army relaunches its offensive into Romania. : 168 Allied airmen arrive at Buchenwald concentration camp .
Nazi collaborator Vidkun Quisling went on trial in Oslo, Norway.

08-22.text: Germans are now shelling Dover and the nearby coastal area with long-range artillery.
German forces close in on Leningrad; the citizens continue improvising fortifications.
Brazil declares war on the Axis countries, partly in response to numerous riots by a populace angry at the sinking of Brazilian ships.

The Japanese are now in total retreat from India. : German Chancellor Adolf Hitler issued the first of several orders to the German commander of Paris, General Dietrich von Choltitz, to destroy the city.
Japanese armies surrender to the Red Army in Manchuria.

08-24.text: German aircraft mistakenly bomb a church in Cripplegate , accidentally dictating the future shape of the Battle of Britain.
The naval battle of the Eastern Solomons; USS Enterprise is badly damaged and the Japanese lose one light carrier, Ryujo .

08-25.text: Churchill orders the bombing of Berlin in retaliation for the previous night's bombing of Cripplegate.
British and Soviet troops invade Iran to save the Abadan oilfields and the important railways and routes to the Soviet Union for the supply of war material.

Paris is liberated ; De Gaulle makes a triumphant speech at the Hotel de la Ville, which is also broadcast nationwide. The German military under Lt. Gen. von Choltitz disobeys Hitler's orders to burn the city and destroy

08-26.text: Both London and Berlin are bombed, Berlin for the first time.
Battle of Milne Bay begins: Japanese forces land and launch a full-scale assault on an Australian base near the eastern tip of New Guinea .
De Gaulle and the Free French parade triumphantly down the Champs-Élysées under some sniper fire.

08-27.text: Douala in French Cameroon is captured by Free France , and soon afterwards the entire colony is captured as well.
German U-boat U-570 , being forced to surface off Iceland is captured by the British Royal Navy and is later put into combat service as HMS Graph .
Marshal Georgii Zhukov is appointed to the command of the Stalingrad defence; the Luftwaffe is now delivering heavy strikes on the city.
Japanese armies in Burma surrender at Rangoon ceremonies.

08-30.text: The bombing of England continues; London is now bombed in retaliation for the bombing of Berlin ; thus, the beginning of "the London Blitz."

Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini dictated the so-called Second Vienna Award which forced Romania to hand over the Northern Transylvania (including the entire Maramureș and part of Crișana ) to Hungary .
The Shetland bus , a clandestine special operations group that made a permanent link between Shetland, Scotland and German-occupied Norway, begins operations.
Beginning of the Yelna Offensive by the Soviet Red Army on the Eastern Front.

The Battle of Alam Halfa , a few miles south of El Alamein begins. This will be Rommel's last attempt to break through the Allied lines in Egypt; the air superiority of the Desert Air Force will play a significant role f
The Allies enter Rouen , in northwestern France.
Royal Navy force under Rear-Admiral Cecil Harcourt liberates Hong Kong .

08-31.text: Luftwaffe attacks on British airfields continue, as well as on London. Attacks on Radar installations prove ineffective.
Two Royal Navy destroyers are sunk off the Dutch coast in the so-called " Texel Disaster ".
The first signs appear that a Leningrad "siege" is beginning.

" The Great Provocation " in Vilnius – German forces stage an attack on their soldiers by Jews, leading to a 'retaliation' mass arrest of the residents of old Jewish quarter, to be murdered at Ponary , three days later.
Start of the 1942 Luxembourgish general strike against conscription.
The Northwest African Air Forces conducts an air raid against the Italian city of Pisa .
American forces turn over the government of France to Free French troops. : The Soviet army enters Bucharest .
General MacArthur takes over command of the Japanese government in Tokyo.

09-09.text: During the Western Desert Campaign , Italian colonial forces in Libya under General Mario Berti launch the invasion of Egypt . The first objective is to advance from defensive positions within Libya to the border with Eg
Tel Aviv in the British Mandate of Palestine is bombed by Italian aircraft causing 137 deaths.
A Japanese plane drops more incendiaries on Oregon, but with little effect.
The Allies land at Salerno, Italy; meanwhile the British troops take Taranto in the heel of the Italian "boot". Allied strategy aims at a "drive" up the "boot". : Iran declares war on Germany.
Charles de Gaulle forms the Provisional Government of the French Republic in France. : The Fatherland Front of Bulgaria overthrows the national government and declares war on Germany.

10-07.text: Responding to a Romanian request made on 7 September, Germany deploys a military mission to Romania to provide training for the Romanian Army and guard the Romanian oilfields.
The Japanese execute 98 American civilians on Wake Island .

10-15.text: Clarence Addison Dykstra becomes Director of Selective Service in the United States.
Mussolini and his closest advisers decide to invade Greece .
Hungarian regent Miklós Horthy is overthrown by the Germans, who replace him with Ferenc Szálasi . : Allied bombardment of Aachen continues, the first major battle on German soil.

10-24.text: After meeting with Franco, Hitler goes to Montoire where a meeting with Philippe Pétain took place signifying the start of organised French collaboration with the Nazi regime.
The Italian Air Corps sees its first action during the Battle of Britain .
In Ukraine , the important mining and industrial centre of Kharkov falls to the German Army Group South forces.
Vilna Ghetto Gelbschein I Aktion. 5,500 Jews including 140 old or paralyzed people killed.

US Navy Task Force 34, consisting of aircraft carriers, a variety of support ships, including troop ships and other vessels, set sail from Hampton Roads, Virginia with Patton's forces for Operation Torch , the landing in

10-25.text: Berlin and Hamburg are bombed heavily.
Rommel hurriedly returns from his sickbed in Germany to take charge of the African battle. (His replacement, General Stumme, had died of a heart attack).

Three distinct air engagements in the Battle of Leyte Gulf take place as U.S. Navy carrier-based planes destroy many Japanese ships in the waters off the Philippines. : Romania is fully liberated by Red Army and Romanian

10-29.text: Very heavy convoy losses during this period as numbers of U-boats increase.
The first number drawings for US Selective Service Act draftees.
Vilna Ghetto II liquidated. 2,500 Jews killed.
The Japanese continue to send troops as reinforcements into Guadalcanal.

11-02.text: The Italian advance into Greece continues. Vovousa is captured and Italian aircraft bomb Salonika .
Political conflict in Yugoslavia as leftists under Tito (Josip Broz) are in competition with the more conservative Serbs under Draža Mihailović .

In the early morning hours, American and Japanese ships fight the inconclusive Battle of Empress Augusta Bay off Bougainville, but the Japanese are unable to land reinforcements. : British troops, in Italy, reach the Gar
Canadian troops take Zeebrugge in Belgium; Belgium is now entirely liberated.

11-07.text: It becomes clear that Ireland will refuse to allow the United Kingdom to use its ports as naval bases.
Heavy RAF night bombings of Berlin, the Ruhr, and Cologne, but with heavy losses.
Election Day in the U.S. : Roosevelt wins an unprecedented, unrepeated fourth term as U.S. president.

11-11.text: British naval forces launch attack against Italian navy at Taranto . Swordfish bombers from HMS  Illustrious damage three battleships, two cruisers and multiple auxiliary craft. The event secures British supply line
Convoys reach Malta from Alexandria; an official announcement proclaims that the island is "relieved of its siege".
American air power continues to hit Rabaul.

11-19.text: The Greeks continue to advance, and evict Italian troops from Greek soil. The Greek counter-offensive
Australian light cruiser HMAS  Sydney and the German auxiliary cruiser  Kormoran sink each other off the coast of Western Australia. All 648 crewmen are lost on HMAS Sydney .
At Stalingrad the Soviet Union forces under General Georgy Zhukov launch Operation Uranus aimed at encircling the Germans in the city and thus turning the tide of battle in the USSR's favor.
Prisoners of the Janowska concentration camp stage a mass escape/uprising when they are ordered to cover up evidence of a mass-murder. Most are rounded up and killed.

11-25.text: The Soviet Union gives her terms to join the Tripartite Pact including substantial new territorial gains for Russia.
U-331 sinks the British battleship HMS  Barham while covering Mediterranean convoys.
In German-occupied Belgium , the Free University of Brussels is closed on the orders of the occupation authorities.
The encirclement of Stalingrad continues to stabilise. Hitler reiterates his demand of Paulus not to surrender.

Americans and Japanese fight the naval Battle of Cape St. George between Buka and New Ireland . Admiral Arleigh Burke's destroyers distinguish themselves. : Rangoon is bombed by American heavy bombers.

Japanese take Nanning in south China, as the war in that theatre continues. : The USS  Intrepid is hit by kamikazes for the third time; other American ships are heavily damaged. : Soviet forces capture Saaremaa isla

12-06.text: 9 December: British and Indian troops of the Western Desert Force launch Operation Compass , an offensive against Italian forces in Egypt. The Italians have seven infantry divisions and the Maletti Group in fortified def
The United Kingdom declares war on Finland.

12-08.text: Francisco Franco rules out Spanish entry into the war; the immediate result is that Hitler is forced to cancel an attack on Gibraltar.
The United States, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and New Zealand declare war on Japan; Roosevelt's Day of Infamy speech .
Japanese forces take the Gilbert Islands (which include Tarawa). Clark Field in the Philippines is bombed, and many American aircraft are destroyed on the ground.
Japanese troops attack Thailand in the Battle of Prachuab Khirikhan .
The Battle of Hong Kong begins.
Kamenka, Krasnaya Polyana , and Kriukovo , are liberated by the Red Army. The Germans are never again within artillery range of Moscow .
The softening-up bombardment of Iwo Jima begins.

12-16.text: The first RAF night raid--on Mannheim, Germany.
In North Africa, the British are in command at Sollum in Egypt and take Fort Capuzzo in Libya.
Rommel orders a withdrawal all the way to El Agheila , where he had begun in March. He awaits reinforcements of men and tanks.
The German offensive around Moscow is now at a complete halt.
Kalinin is retaken in a large Red Army offensive.
The Battle of the Bulge begins as German forces attempt a breakthrough in the Ardennes region. The main object of Hitler's plan is the retaking of Antwerp.

12-22.text: The Japanese land at Lingayan Gulf , on the northern part of Luzon in the Philippines.
Start of the Arcadia Conference in Washington, D.C., the first official meeting of British and American political and military leaders.
The Germans begin a retreat from the Caucasus.

The battle for Bastogne is at its height, with soldiers of the 101st Airborne Division running low on ammunition, food and other vital supplies. Brigadier General Anthony McAuliffe 's famous "Nuts!" reply is sent to Germ

12-29.text: Large German air-raids on London; St Paul's Cathedral is damaged.
Control of the Andaman Islands is handed over to Azad Hind by the Japanese.
Soviet troops begin the Siege of Budapest .

01-03.text: RAF bombers attack Bremen and the Kiel Canal in Germany. The Kiel Canal Bridge suffers a direct hit and collapses on Finnish ship Yrsa .
Major Gregory Pappy Boyington , the USMC fighter ace, was shot down after downing the last 3 of his 26 victories, and would spend the next 20 months in Japanese POW Camps.
The Allies take the offensive east of the Bulge but they fail to close the pincers (which might have surrounded large numbers of Germans) with Patton's tanks.

01-05.text: Operation Compass : Australian troops of XIII Corps (the re-designated Western Desert Force ) capture Italian-held Bardia and 45,000 Italian prisoners are taken. Tobruk, the next target, is 70 miles away.
The leader of Wallonia 's fascist party, Léon Degrelle , gives a speech in the German-occupied city of Liège announcing the support of the Rexist Party for German Nazism.
The beginning of a major Red Army offensive under General Zhukov .

Eighteen countries issue a declaration in London stating their determination to "combat and defeat the plundering by the enemy Powers of the territories which have been overrun or brought under enemy control" and to take
The German offensive Nordwind crosses the border into Alsace . : Japanese retreat across the Irrawaddy River in Burma with General Slim 's troops in pursuit.

01-06.text: The Greeks advance towards Klisura Pass .
The British advance continues to El Agheila , on the western edge of Libya.

01-11.text: In London, 57 people are killed and 69 injured when a German bomb lands outside the Bank of England , demolishing the Underground station below and leaving a 120-foot crater.
Japanese troops capture Kuala Lumpur, Malaya.
The first convoy moves on the Ledo Road (or "Stilwell" road) in northern Burma, linking India and China.

01-12.text: Operation Compass : British and Australian troops of XIII Corps prepare for the assault on Italian-held Tobruk .
The SS United Victory , the first Victory ship , is launched; this class of transport will prove to be crucial in hauling men and supplies across the oceans.
The East Prussian Offensive , a major Red Army offensive in East Prussia , begins on January 13th. The Soviet Vistula-Oder Offensive begins. Its goal is to capture Poland and Eastern Germany.

01-13.text: Heavy Luftwaffe night raid on Plymouth.
The Red Army takes Kirov and Medya, as its counter-offensive continues.
1st Byelorussian Front launched its winter offensive towards Pillkallen, East Prussia, meeting heavy resistance from the German 3rd Panzer Army .

01-14.text: First use of " V for Victory " by Victor de Laveleye on the BBC 's Belgian service, Radio Belgique .

The Casablanca Conference of Allied leaders begins. Winston Churchill and Franklin D. Roosevelt discuss the eventual invasion of mainland Europe, the impending invasion of Sicily and Italy, and the wisdom of the principl
British forces clear the Roer Triangle during Operation Blackcock ; it is an area noted for its industrial dams.

01-15.text: The rivalry between Chinese Nationalists and Chinese Communists becomes more evident; large numbers of the latter are forced to give up their arms.
German authorities begin to deport Jews from the Lodz ghettos to the Chelmno Concentration Camp.
The British start an offensive aimed at taking far-off Tripoli, Libya .

The British commander in Athens, General Ronald Scobie , accepts a request for a ceasefire from the Greek People's Liberation Army . This marks the end of the Dekemvriana , resulting in clear defeat for the Greek Left.

01-18.text: Air raids on Malta are increasing in focus and intensity.
The Jews in the Warsaw Ghetto rise up for the first time, starting the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising . : Besieged defenders of Leningrad link up with relieving forces.

01-19.text: The 4th and 5th Indian Divisions continue the British counter-offensive in East Africa , attacking Italian-held Eritrea from the Sudan .
Hitler and Mussolini meet at Berchtesgaden; Hitler agrees to provide aid in North Africa.
Japanese forces take large numbers of British troops prisoner, north of Singapore.
General Georgy Zhukov is promoted to Marshal as the Stalingrad struggle grinds to a close.
Red Army troops push westward toward the Baltic countries. : British Operation Outward accidentally claims lives in Sweden by knocking out lighting and causing a train crash.
Hitler orders that any retreats of divisions or larger units must be approved by him.

01-23.text: HMS Illustrious , heavily damaged, leaves Malta for repairs in Alexandria.
Charles Lindbergh testifies before the U.S. Congress and recommends that the United States negotiate a neutrality pact with Adolf Hitler .
The Battle of Rabaul , on New Britain begins.

British capture Tripoli, Libya. : Japanese continue their fight in western Guadalcanal ; although facing setbacks in Papua, they resolve to continue the fight and to attempt sporadic air attacks on Allied forces in the r
The British destroyer HMS  Janus is sunk off Anzio.
German jurist and anti-Nazi activist Helmuth James von Moltke was hanged for treason in Berlin.

01-29.text: Death of the Greek dictator, Ioannis Metaxas .
Rommel's Afrika Korps recaptures Benghazi, Libya in his drive east. For the next few months, the two sides will rest and rearm.
The naval battle of Rennell Island , near Guadalcanal, begins. The Japanese beat the Americans and the USS  Chicago is lost.

01-30.text: British forces in North Africa take Derna ; 100 miles west of Tobruk.
Hitler speaks at the Berlin Sportpalast and threatens the Jews of the world with annihilation; he also blames the failure of the offensive in The Soviet Union on the weather.

The last Japanese have cleared out of Guadalcanal undetected by U.S. forces. : On the tenth anniversary of his rise to power, Hitler makes a speech in which he promotes General Paulus to Field Marshal. This includes a re

The Malta Conference (1945) began with Winston Churchill meeting with the Combined Chiefs of Staff on the Island of Malta in the Mediterranean to plan the end of WWII in both Theaters, and to discuss the ramifications of

01-31.text: Indian 4th Division flanks and then captures Agordat, Eritrea, Italian East Africa. 1,000 Italian troops and 43 field guns are captured.
The Japanese take the port of Moulamein, Burma; they now threaten Rangoon as well as Singapore.

Friedrich Paulus ( Generalfeldmarschall in command of the German 6th Army ) and his staff surrender to Soviet troops in Stalingrad, the first time a German Field Marshal is lost to surrender and thus captured by the enem
Operation Flintlock began, as American forces land on Kwajalein Atoll and other islands in the Japanese -held Marshall Islands . United States troops also invade Majuro, Marshall Islands .

The Red Army crosses the Oder River into Germany and are now less than 50 miles from Berlin. : A second invasion on Luzon by Americans lands on the west coast. : The whole Burma Road is now opened as the Ledo Road linkag

02-03.text: Lieutenant-General Erwin Rommel is appointed head of "German Army troops in Africa." This unit is later to be officially designated as the " Afrika Korps ".
Germany forcibly restores Pierre Laval to office in Vichy .
Japanese air power conducts airstrikes against Java , especially the naval base at Surabaya .
American planes bomb Eniwetok in the Marshalls, later to be a major B-29 base.

02-07.text: Operation Compass : After several days of desperate fighting, a flying column of XIII Corps called Combe Force cuts off the retreating Italian 10th Army during the Battle of Beda Fomm. The Italians are unable to break th
Americans continue their defence of Bataan against General Homma's troops.
In the United States, it is announced that shoe rationing will go into effect in two days.
In a radio interview, the last Estonian Prime Minister Jüri Uluots , as acting Head of State, supports mobilisation.
Paraguay declares war on Germany and Japan.

02-08.text: US House of Representatives passes the Lend-Lease bill.
The Chindits (a "long range penetration group") under British General Orde Wingate begin an incursion into Burma. : United States' VI Corps arrives in North Africa.
The plan for the invasion of France, Operation Overlord , is confirmed.

02-11.text: Elements of the Afrika Korps start to arrive in Tripoli , Tripolitania .

The " Channel Dash " – The German battleships Scharnhorst and Gneisenau , with the heavy cruiser Prinz Eugen , rush out of Brest through the English Channel to northern ports, including Wilhelmshaven, Germany; the Britis
U.S. General Dwight D. Eisenhower is selected to command the Allied armies in Europe.
In the battle of Korsun–Cherkassy, German forces sent to relieve the Korsun pocket in Ukraine are now only 10 miles away.

02-19.text: The start of the "three nights Blitz" of Swansea , South Wales . Over these three nights of intensive bombing, Swansea town centre is almost completely obliterated.
Japanese aircraft attack Darwin , in Australia's Northern Territory .
Leipzig , Germany is bombed for two straight nights. This marks the beginning of a " Big Week " bombing campaign against German industrial cities by Allied bombers.

02-20.text: German and British troops confront each other for the first time in North Africa—at El Agheila in western Libya.
Japanese troops cross the important Salween River in Burma.
A colonial military garrison in Luluabourg in the Belgian Congo mutinies, killing three.

02-24.text: German U-boat offensive in the Atlantic is now increasingly successful.
Admiral Darlan is appointed the head of the Vichy government in France.
Egypt declares war on the Axis. Moments after making this Declaration before Parliament, Prime Minister Ahmad Maher Pasha is assassinated.

02-25.text: The British submarine HMS  Upright sinks the Italian cruiser Armando Diaz in one of the numerous sea battles in the North African campaign.
Mogadishu , the capital of Italian Somaliland , is captured by British forces during the East African Campaign .
The internment of Japanese-American citizens in the Western United States begins as fears of invasion increase.
Taking off on the 24th, a US B-29 incendiary raid on Tokyo, Japan takes place.

02-28.text: Operation Gunnerside : six Norwegians led by Joachim Rønneberg successfully attack the heavy water plant Vemork .
Belgian industrialist Alexandre Galopin is assassinated in occupied Belgium by Flemish paramilitaries.
A Philippine government is established. : U.S. and Filipino forces invade Palawan , an island of the Philippines.

03-04.text: British commandos carry out an attack on oil facilities at Narvik in Norway.
British military force in Libya is thinned down as some men are sent to assist the Greeks in their emerging battle with approaching German troops.
Prince Regent Paul of Yugoslavia agrees to join the Axis pact.
Japanese naval Operation K occurs, intended as a reconnaissance of Pearl Harbor and disruption of repair and salvage operations.

Winston Churchill told the House of Commons the Allies intended to completely isolate Ireland to prevent military secrets from leaking to the Axis, hinting the border with Northern Ireland would soon be closed. 30 Royal

03-07.text: First British troops land in Greece, at Piraeus.
Japanese begin an invasion attempt on India, starting a four-month battle around Imphal .

The Battle of Remagen : When German troops fail to dynamite the Ludendorff Bridge over the Rhine, the U.S. First Army captures the bridge and begins crossing the river. The Army also takes Cologne , Germany. : Germans be

03-08.text: Another bombing of London, notable because Buckingham Palace is hit.
The Japanese land at Lae and Salamaua , on Huon Bay, New Guinea, beginning their move toward Port Moresby, New Guinea, and then Australia.
Continuing German counter-attacks around Kharkov. : Nuremberg is heavily bombed.

American forces are attacked by Japanese troops on Hill 700 in Bougainville ; the battle will last five days. : A Red Army offensive on a wide front west of the Dnieper in Ukraine forces the Germans into a major retreat.
Private Karl Hulten, an Army Airborne Regiment deserter, was hanged in an English prison for a flurry of crimes ending in what came to be called the Cleft chin murder .

03-09.text: The Italian Spring Offensive in the Albanian front begins.
Japanese troops entered Rangoon , Burma, which was abandoned by the British two days earlier. It appears that the Japanese are in control of Java, Burma, and New Guinea.

Members of the Calcutta Light Horse carry out a covert attack against a German merchantship, which had been transmitting Allied positions to U-boats from the Mormugao Harbour in neutral Portugal's protectorate, the India
The Soviet Long Range Aviation carries out an air raid on Tallinn , Estonia. The military targets are almost untouched. Approx. 800 civilians die and 20,000 people are left without shelter.

The US firebombs Tokyo (the attack was code-named Operation Meetinghouse ), with heavy civilian casualties. : Amid rumours of a possible American invasion, Japanese overthrow the Vichy French Jean Decoux Government which

03-10.text: British and Italian troops meet in a brief conflict in Eritrea.
Portsmouth suffers heavy casualties after another night of heavy bombing by the Luftwaffe.
The USAAF 14th Air Force is formed in China, under General Claire Lee Chennault , former head of the " Flying Tigers ". : The US House of Representatives votes to extend the Lend-Lease plan.
The creation of the Political Committee of National Liberation in Greece .
Japanese Fu-Go balloon bombs damage the Manhattan Project's Hanford Site in Washington State slightly, but cause no lasting effects.

03-13.text: The Luftwaffe strikes with a large force at Glasgow and the shipping industry along the River Clyde .
RAF launches an air raid against Essen, Germany.
German forces liquidate the Jewish ghetto in Kraków .
On Bougainville , Japanese troops end their failed assault on American forces at Hill 700.

03-17.text: Huge convoy losses in mid-Atlantic this week.
The United States of America converts its Corps Areas to Defense Commands, with the term Corps reassigned as an intermediate field command of a Field Army.
U.S. General Douglas MacArthur arrives in Australia, after leaving his headquarters in the Philippines.
Devastating convoy losses in the Atlantic due to increased U-boat activity; the middle of the Atlantic is apparently not sufficiently covered by planes or ships.

03-19.text: The worst bombing of London so far this year, with heavy damage from incendiary bombs; Plymouth and Bristol are bombed again.
German forces occupy Hungary in Operation Margarethe . : Yugoslav partisans attack Trieste, on the border of Italy and Slovenia.

03-20.text: The Italian Spring Offensive is called off, after heavy losses and virtually no progress.
Operation Outward begins, a program to attack Germany by means of free-flying balloons.
Montgomery 's forces begin a breakthrough in Tunisia, striking at the Mareth line.
Red Army advances in Ukraine continue with great success.

German General Gotthard Heinrici replaces Heinrich Himmler as commander of Army Group Vistula , the army group directly opposing the Soviet advance towards Berlin. : Mandalay liberated by the Indian 19th Infantry Divisio

03-24.text: Rommel attacks and reoccupies El Agheila , Libya in his first offensive. The British retreat and within three weeks are driven back to Egypt.
Operation Varsity , an Anglo-American-Canadian airborne assault under Montgomery deployed over the Rhine at Wesel.

03-25.text: Italian MTMs of the Decima MAS sink the heavy cruiser HMS  York  (90) , a large tanker (the Norwegian Pericles ), another tanker and a cargo ship in Suda Bay , Crete .
RAF sends bomber raids against targets in France and Germany.
Soviet air force bombs the city of Tartu , Estonia.

03-27.text: Crown Prince Peter becomes Peter II of Yugoslavia and takes control of Yugoslavia after an army coup overthrows the pro-German government of the Prince Regent.
Japanese spy Takeo Yoshikawa arrives in Honolulu, Hawaii and begins to study the United States fleet at Pearl Harbor .
Hitler orders his military leaders to plan for the invasion of Yugoslavia.
British forces advancing from the Sudan win the decisive Battle of Keren in Eritrea.
Battle of Cape Matapan : the British navy meets an Italian fleet off southern Greece. The battle continues until the 29th.

The Western Allies slow their advance and allow the Red Army to take Berlin. : Argentina declares war on Germany, the last Western hemisphere country to do so; its policies for sheltering escaping Nazis are also coming u

03-31.text: The Afrika Korps continues the German offensive in North Africa; Mersa Brega , north of El Agheila , is taken.
General Eisenhower broadcasts a demand for the Germans to surrender.

04-01.text: British retreat after the losses at El Agheila, Libya. Rommel is surprised, then decides to continue his offensive.
During this month the heavy bombing of British cities continues, and convoy losses remain heavy.

In Iraq , pro- German Rashid Ali and other members of the " Golden Square " stage a military coup d'état and overthrow the regime of the pro-British Regent 'Abd al-Ilah . Rashid Ali names himself Chief of a "National Def

The Eastern Sea Frontier , desperately short on suitable escort vessels after the Destroyers for Bases Agreement , institutes an interim arrangement known as the "Bucket Brigaid," wherein vessels outside of protected har
Allies continue to squeeze the Germans into the corner of Tunisia.
U.S. troops start Operation Iceberg , which is the Battle of Okinawa . It would have been a leaping off base for a mainland invasion . : Americans retake Legaspi , Albay in the Philippines.

04-02.text: After taking Agedabia, Rommel decides to take all of Libya and moves his troops toward Benghazi. All of Cyrenaica (Libya) seems ready for the taking.
Over 24,000 sick and starving troops (American and Filipino) are now trapped on the Bataan Peninsula .
Soviets launch the Vienna Offensive against German forces in and around the Austrian capital city. : German armies are surrounded in the Ruhr Pocket .

04-04.text: Rommel is now about 200 miles east of El Agheila, heading for Tobruk and Egypt.
An Atlantic convoy suffers almost 50% losses to U-boat campaign.
Germans plan "Baedeker raids" on touristy or historic British sites, in revenge for the Lübeck bombing.

The only large-scale escape of Allied prisoners-of-war from the Japanese in the Pacific takes place when ten American POWs and two Filipino convicts break out of the Davao Penal Colony on the island of Mindanao in the so
General Charles de Gaulle takes command of all Free French forces.

Bratislava , the capital of the Slovak Republic , is overrun by advancing Soviet forces. The remaining members of President Jozef Tiso 's pro-German government flee to Austria. : The Ohrdruf death camp is liberated by th

04-06.text: Forces of Germany, Italy, and Hungary, moving through Romania and Hungary, initiate the invasions of Yugoslavia and Greece .
The Italian Army is driven out from Addis Ababa , Ethiopia.
The northern wing of Rommel's forces take Derna, on the Libyan coast. The southern wing moves toward Mechili , and takes it on the 8th.
Japanese naval forces put troops ashore on Manus Island in the Bismarck Archipelago (some sources give a date of 8 April for these landings).
The Japanese drive on the Plain of Imphal , supposedly halted, proves strong enough to surround British forces at Imphal and Kohima , in India.
The Spring 1945 offensive in Italy begins in northern Italy.

04-07.text: The Luftwaffe begins a two-day assault on Belgrade, Yugoslavia; Hitler is infuriated by the Yugoslav resistance.

Hitler and Mussolini come together at Salzburg , mostly for the purpose of propping up Mussolini's fading morale. : Allied forces–the Americans from the West, the British from the East–link up near Gafsa in Tunisia. : Bo
The Japanese battleship Yamato is sunk in the waters north of Okinawa as the Japanese make their last major naval operation .

04-08.text: The Red Army attacks in an attempt to retake all of the Crimea, the Germans retreat westward to Sevastopol.

04-13.text: Malta is bombed again; it continues to be a thorn in the side of German supply movements in the Mediterranean.
Japan and the Soviet Union sign a neutrality pact .
In Iraq, a small contingent of British reinforcements are air-lifted to RAF Shaibah .

04-17.text: Yugoslavia surrenders. A government in exile is formed in London. King Peter escapes to Greece.

French General Henri Giraud , who was captured in 1940, escapes from a castle prison at Königstein by lowering himself down the castle wall and jumping on board a moving train, which takes him to the French border.
Japanese launch Operation Ichi-Go with over 600,000 men in central China. The objective is to conquer areas where American bombers are located. The first phase is the Battle of Central Henan .
The Italian town of Montese is liberated by Brazilian forces after four-day Battle of Montese .

04-18.text: Greek Prime Minister Alexandros Koryzis commits suicide; the British plan the major evacuation of Greece.
In Iraq, in accordance with the Anglo-Iraqi Treaty , British forces from India start to land at Basra .
Doolittle Raid on Nagoya , Tokyo and Yokohama . Jimmy Doolittle 's B-25s take off from USS  Hornet . The raids are a great boost of morale for Americans.
Ernie Pyle , famed war correspondent for the GIs, is killed by machine gun fire on Ie Shima , a small island near Okinawa.

Beginning of so-called Baedeker Raids by the Luftwaffe on English provincial towns like Exeter, Bath, Norwich, and York; attacks continue sporadically until June 6.

Hermann Göring sends a radiogram to Hitler's bunker, asking to be declared Hitler's successor. He proclaims that if he gets no response by 10 PM, he will assume Hitler is incapacitated and assume leadership of the Reich.

04-24.text: British and Australian forces evacuate from Greece to Crete and Egypt.
Plymouth suffers the third night of heavy bombing by the Luftwaffe.
Heavy bombing of Rostock , Germany by RAF.
British troops force open the road from Imphal to Kohima in India .

04-25.text: Rommel wins an important victory at Halfaya Pass, close to the Egyptian border.
Axis forces defeat Commonwealth forces at Thermopylae after Australian general George Vasey staunchly claims that they will not be beaten.

Elbe Day : First contact between Soviet and American troops at the river Elbe , near Torgau in Germany.

04-26.text: Rommel attacks the Gazala defence line and crosses into Egypt; Tobruk continues to hold however.
Hitler assumes a kind of supreme authority over Germany.
The British finally take "Longstop Hill" in Tunisia, a key position on the breakout road to Tunis.

Hitler summons Field Marshal Robert Ritter von Greim from Munich to Berlin to take over command of the Luftwaffe from Göring. While flying into Berlin, von Greim is seriously wounded by Soviet anti-aircraft fire.

04-30.text: Rommel is ordered to cease attacks on Tobruk after another failure.
In Iraq , Iraqi armed forces occupy the plateau to the south of the RAF Habbaniya air base and inform the base commander that all flying should cease immediately.

In response to American intelligence intercepts, which warn of the impending Japanese landings, the Australian garrison is evacuated from Tulagi .
Japanese aircraft again bomb Darwin , Australia.

Rangoon is liberated. : The German cruiser Admiral Hipper is scuttled, having been hit heavily by the RAF in April.

05-04.text: Belfast, Northern Ireland, experiences another heavy bombing by the Luftwaffe.
US Rear Admiral Frank Jack Fletcher 's Task Force 17 makes the first carrier strike of the Battle of the Coral Sea , attacking Japanese naval targets near Tulagi .
Karl Dönitz orders all U-boats to cease operations. : German troops in Denmark, Northern Germany and The Netherlands surrender to Montgomery . : Neuengamme concentration camp is liberated.

05-06.text: With much of the Iraqi air force destroyed and facing regular bombardment themselves, the Iraqi ground forces besieging RAF Habbaniya withdraw.
The Luftwaffe arranges to send a small force to Iraq.

On Corregidor , Lt. General Jonathan M. Wainwright surrenders the last U.S. forces in the Philippines to Lt. General Masaharu Homma . About 12,000 are made prisoners. Homma will soon face criticism from his superiors ove
Heavy Allied bombings of the Continent in preparation for D-Day.

The Italian Viceroy in Ethiopia surrenders. Remnants of Italian troops keep on fighting.
Increased Allied bombing of targets in France in preparation for D-Day.

05-22.text: Iraqi forces unsuccessfully counter-attack the British forces in Fallujah and are rebuffed.
Mexico declares war on the Axis.
Allies bomb Sicily and Sardinia, both possible landing sites.

05-27.text: The German battleship Bismarck is sunk in the North Atlantic by the Royal Navy, after evasive tactics, and a damaged steering system which forced it into an endless series of circular movements.
The British forces from the Habbaniya area begin an advance on Baghdad and, within four days, approach the city from the west and from the north.
Twelve Italian aircraft arrive at Mosul to join Fliegerführer Irak .
1941 Nord-Pas-de-Calais miners' strike breaks out in German-occupied Northern France.
Reinhard Heydrich , head of the Reich Security Main Office , is fatally wounded in Prague during Operation Anthropoid by Czechoslovak soldiers; he would die on June 4 from his wounds.
Operation Horlicks starts, as Americans land on Biak , Dutch New Guinea, a key Japanese air base; stubborn Japanese resistance until August.

05-29.text: Members of the German military mission flee Iraq.
The Jews in France are ordered to wear the yellow Star of David.
RAF bombs Wuppertal , causing heavy civilian losses.
Fighting breaks out in Syria and Lebanon, as nationalists demand freedom from French control.

06-01.text: Commonwealth forces complete the withdrawal from Crete .
Rationing of clothes begins in the United Kingdom.
First reports in the West that gas is being used to kill the Jews sent to "the East".

06-02.text: Tuskegee Airmen begin with the formation of the 99th Fighter Squadron.
Further heavy bombing of industrial sites in Germany, centred mainly on Essen.
The U.S. begins Operation Frantic with a bombing of Debrecen , Hungary.
Air Group 87 aircraft from USS Ticonderoga strike airfields on Kyushu , Japan, in an attempt to stop special attack aircraft from taking off.

06-06.text: More British fighter planes are delivered to Malta; Luftwaffe attacks continue.

06-08.text: Vichy French-controlled Syria and Lebanon are invaded by Australian, British, Free French, and Indian forces.
Malta receives a squadron of Spitfires .
Japanese forces begin to evacuate Kiska Island in the Aleutians, their last foothold in the Western hemisphere. The event is almost to the year of their landing.

The National Committee of the Republic of Estonia makes a declaration "to the Estonian People." The declaration was made public to the world press in Stockholm in July 1944 and in Tallinn on 1 August 1944.

07-07.text: British and Canadian troops in Iceland are replaced by Americans.
Walter Dornberger briefs the V-2 rocket to Hitler, who approves the project for top priority.

07-08.text: Yugoslavia, a country formed by the Versailles treaty, is dissolved by the Axis into its component parts; especially important will be Croatia, with a pro-Axis government.
Britain and the USSR sign a mutual defence agreement, promising not to sign any form of separate peace agreement with Germany.

07-13.text: Montenegro starts an uprising against the Axis Powers shortly after the Royalists in Serbia begin theirs. Questionable Communist plans instigate parallel uprising and civil war.
Hitler calls off the Kursk offensive, but the Soviets continue the battle.
The Soviets take Vilnius, Lithuania. : The Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive begins.

07-15.text: The Red Army starts a counter-attack against the Wehrmacht near Leningrad.
Argentia naval air base is set up in Newfoundland; it will prove an important transfer station for the Allies for some years.
The only action around El Alamein is light skirmishing.

07-17.text: Luftwaffe air attacks on Malta continue.
Field Marshal Rommel is badly wounded when his car is strafed from the air in France.

The Potsdam Conference begins under British Prime Minister Churchill , Soviet Prime Minister Stalin and U.S. President Truman . The Allied leaders agree to insist upon the unconditional surrender of Japan.

07-20.text: Heinrich Himmler visits Soviet POWs near Minsk and Lublin and decides to build the concentration camp near Lublin known as Majdanek concentration camp .

Lewis B. Hershey succeeds Clarence Dykstra as Director of the Selective Service System in the United States.
U.S. conducts air attacks on the cities of Kobe and Nagoya in Japan.

08-07.text: Germans reach the Gulf of Finland , cutting the Soviet forces in Estonia into two, with the forces in Tallinn being detached from the rest of Soviet lines.
Operation Watchtower begins the Guadalcanal Campaign as American forces invade Gavutu , Guadalcanal , Tulagi and Tanambogo in the Solomon Islands .
First trials of the bomb conspirators against Hitler begin in a court presided over by notorious Judge Roland Freisler .

08-09.text: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill meet at NS Argentia , Newfoundland . The Atlantic Charter is created, signed, and released to the world press.
Numerous riots in favour of independence in India; Mahatma Gandhi is arrested.
President Roosevelt chooses General Douglas MacArthur 's plan to invade the Philippines and turns down Admiral Chester W. Nimitz 's plan to invade Taiwan .
The B-29 bomber Bockscar drops the second atomic bomb " Fat Man " on Nagasaki .

08-12.text: Hitler, against the advice of his generals, shifts some forces from the Moscow front to Leningrad and the Crimean offensives.
At a conference in Moscow, Churchill informs Stalin that there will not be a "second front" in 1942.

Incendiary bombs dropped by a Japanese seaplane cause a forest fire in Oregon .
The Germans surrender at Toulon and Marseille in southern France. : Patton's tanks cross the Marne .

10-22.text: 35,000 Jews are expelled to the Slobodka Ghetto and are left in freezing conditions for 10 days. Many perish in the cold.
Conscription age in Britain reduced to 18.

11-18.text: Operation Crusader : British Commonwealth and other Allied troops cross into Libya and at least temporarily relieve the Siege of Tobruk .
Heavy British RAF raid on Berlin with few losses.
440 Royal Air Force planes bomb Berlin causing only light damage and killing 131. The RAF lose nine aircraft and 53 aviators.

11-28.text: Battle of Rostov – Rostov-on-Don is recaptured by the Red Army.
Battle of Moscow – German Panzers are on the outskirts of Moscow, near the Moscow-Volga Canal.
The last Italian armed forces in East Africa surrender at Gondar .

General strike begins among native mine-workers in the Belgian Congo .
Vilna Ghetto 'Criminal Aktion' begins, continued the next day. 157 Jews are killed at Ponary.

The Marines turn over Guadalcanal to the American army.

Italian " human torpedoes " damage two British battleships, HMS  Queen Elizabeth and HMS  Valiant in Alexandria harbour.
HMS  Neptune , leading Force K , strikes a minefield and sinks with one survivor and a loss of 766 crew.

12-21.text: The suffering of besieged Leningrad continues; it is estimated that about 3,000 are dying each day of starvation and various diseases.

12-23.text: A second Japanese landing attempt on Wake Island is successful, and the American garrison surrenders after hours of fighting.
General MacArthur declares Manila an open city .
Japanese air force planes begin bombing of Calcutta.
The skies clear over the Ardennes, permitting Allied aircraft to begin their attacks on the German offensive, the one factor that Hitler feared in his planning.

12-25.text: Red Army and Navy amphibious forces land at Kerch , in Crimea ; the Battle of the Kerch Peninsula will last through April.

12-26.text: Heavy fighting continues on Guadalcanal, now focused on Mount Austen in the west.
German battleship Scharnhorst is sunk off North Cape (in the Arctic) by a British force led by the battleship HMS  Duke of York .
American Marines land on Cape Gloucester, New Britain.

The siege of Bastogne is broken by Patton's Third Army tanks, and with it the Ardennes offensive collapses into failure. : Racial tensions within the US military boil over into the Agana race riot on Guam .

01-08.text: Japanese troops penetrated the outer lines of defense at Kuala Lumpur , Malaya .
The battle of Strasbourg is underway, with Americans in defence of their recent acquisition.

01-09.text: Japanese advances in Borneo met with little opposition.
United States Western Task Force redesignated I Armored Corps .
British forces take Maungdaw , Burma, a critical port for Allied supplies.
Americans land on Luzon . There are more kamikaze attacks on the American navy.

01-25.text: Thailand declares war on the United States and United Kingdom.
United States XIV Corps arrives in Pacific Theater.
The American navy bombards Iwo Jima in preparation for an invasion.

01-26.text: The first American forces arrive in Europe landing in Northern Ireland .

01-28.text: Brazil breaks off relations with the Axis powers.
A new conscription law in Germany: men between 16 and 65 and women between 17 and 50 are open to mobilization. : Georgy Zhukov awarded the first Order of Suvorov 1st Class.

The Red Army completes the occupation of Lithuania .

Ecuador declares war on Germany and Japan. : Naval docks at Singapore are destroyed by B-29 attacks.

Rommel launches a counter-attack against the Americans in western Tunisia; he takes Sidi Bouzid and Gafsa . The Battle of the Kasserine Pass begins: inexperienced American troops are soon forced to retreat.
The Battle of Budapest ends with Soviet victory, after a long defense by the Germans.

02-22.text: President Franklin Delano Roosevelt orders General Douglas MacArthur to evacuate the Philippines as American defense of the nation collapses.
Japanese POWs refuse to work at Featherston prisoner of war camp ; this escalates into a deadly clash between the inmates and the guards.
John P. Lucas is replaced as commander of the U.S. VI Corps by Major General Lucian Truscott at Anzio.
Operation Clarion , a massive bombing of German rail and other transport infrastructure by approximately 9,000 U.S. and British aircraft takes place, carrying over into 23 February.

USS  Cod sinks a Japanese merchant ship by torpedo.
Lebanon declares war on Germany and Japan

Battle of Medenine , Tunisia. It is Rommel's last battle in Africa as he is forced to retreat.

03-14.text: Japanese land troops in the Solomon Islands , underscoring Australia's dangerous situation, especially if, as it is soon made clear, an airfield is built on Guadalcanal.

03-22.text: A fractured convoy reaches Malta, after heavy losses to the Luftwaffe and an Italian sea force. Continued heavy bombing attacks on the island with slight opposition from overtaxed RAF air forces.
Japanese forces cross the Indian border all along the Imphal front. : Frankfurt is bombed with heavy civilian losses.
23: US and British forces cross the Rhine at Oppenheim.

US Air Force bombs Ploiești oil fields in Romania, with heavy losses.

Allies attempt to close the mid-Atlantic gap in the war against the U-boats with long-range bombers.

The Dumbarton Oaks Conference begins, setting up the basic structure of the United Nations.

Operation Polkovodets Rumyantsev liberates Kharkov , Ukraine. The Battle of Kursk has become the first successful major Soviet summer offensive of the war.
Romania breaks with the Axis, surrenders to the Soviet Union, and joins the Allies.

V-2 rockets continue to hit Britain, at the rate of about eight a day.

US navy air attacks on Formosa ( Taiwan )
